nodes.procedure: CuNiFe₁@CF was prepared by one-step cathodic electrodeposition on copper foam using deposition solution containing metal salts with Fe:Ni:Cu molar ratio corresponding to X=1, sodium acetate as conductive agent, in electrolyte with KOH and NaCl, resulting in dendritic structure with active phases Fe_{0.64}Ni_{0.36} and FeOOH nanosheet-covered surface.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images show large dendritic structure in region 1 and microdendritic structures of microsphere accumulation in region 2, both with nanosheeted surfaces.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Region 1 on CuNiFe₁@CF shows a large dendritic structure, and region 2 CuNiFe₁@CF exhibits microdendritic structures of microsphere accumulation in Figure S3.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM confirms dendritic and microdendritic surfaces are both nanosheeted structures.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure1a-c shows that the dendritic and microdendritic surfaces of regions 1 and 2 are both nanosheeted structures and can therefore be considered as dendritic structures within both regions.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows lattice stripe spacings of 0.207 nm corresponding to (111) crystal plane of Fe₀.₆₄Ni₀.₃₆ and 0.246 nm corresponding to (200) crystal plane of FeOOH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The lattice stripe spacings of 0.207 nm correspond to the (111) crystal plane of Fe₀.₆₄Ni₀.₃₆. The lattice stripe spacings of 0.246 nm correspond to the (200) crystal plane of FeOOH.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS elemental mapping shows Fe, Ni, Cu, and O uniformly dispersed in nanosheet flower structure; Fe and Ni contents significantly higher than Cu and O in region 1.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fe, Ni, Cu, and O were uniformly dispersed in the nanosheet flower structure. However, the Fe and Ni contents are significantly higher than those of Cu and O in region 1.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD of CuNiFe₁@CF corresponds to Fe₀.₆₄Ni₀.₃₆ (PDF no. 47-1705), matching HRTEM results.
nodes.evidence_snippet: CuNiFe₁@CF corresponds to Fe₀.₆₄Ni₀.₃₆ (PDF no. 47-1705), which also closely matches the HRTEM test.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman shows main peak ~556 cm⁻¹ corresponding to FeOOH; confirms active material contains Fe₀.₆₄Ni₀.₃₆ and FeOOH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The main peak ~556 cm⁻¹ in the Raman spectrum of CuNiFe₁@CF corresponds to the FeOOH substances. The analysis results of XRD and Raman characterization confirmed that the CuNiFe₁@CF catalyst active material contained Fe₀.₆₄Ni₀.₃₆ and FeOOH.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS of CuNiFe₁@CF shows Fe 2p peaks at 710.47/723.61 eV (Fe²⁺), 712.11/725.50 eV (Fe³⁺ in FeOOH); Ni 2p with lower Ni³⁺ binding energy indicating electronic structure optimization; Cu 2p showing Cu⁰ presence; O 1s indicating oxygen vacancies.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2e shows the Fe 2p spectrum, and for CuNiFe₁@CF, two distinct peaks at 718.05 and 732.82 eV match the satellite peaks of Fe 2p₃/₂ and 2p₁/₂, respectively. The other two pairs of peaks 710.47 eV/723.61 and 712.11/725.50 eV belong to Fe oxides (Fe²⁺ and Fe³⁺, respectively). 712.11 and 725.50 eV can be attributed to FeOOH... Figure 2d displays the Ni 2p pattern... The binding energy of Ni³⁺ in the CuNiFe₁@CF catalyst is significantly lower... Figure 2c and f shows the XPS spectra of Cu 2p and O 1s... In particular, Cu⁰ is present in the CuNiFe₁@CF catalyst... The XPS of O 1s shows that the deposition process generates many oxygen vacancies.

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-reaction XRD of CuNiFe₁@CF shows peaks at 31.9° and 51.6° (NiOOH, PDF no. 06-0075) and 36.2°, 36.5°, 40.7°, 44.8°, 52.3°, 59.9°, 64.5°, 65.9° (FeOOH, PDF no. 26-0792).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 5h shows the XRD characterization before and after the HER and OER reactions. The reaction occurs with distinctive peaks at 31.9 and 51.6°, which are attributed to NiOOH (PDF no. 06-0075), and at 36.2, 36.5, 40.7, 44.8, 52.3, 59.9, 64.5, and 65.9°, which are attributed to FeOOH (PDF no. 26-0792).

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-reaction Raman of CuNiFe₁@CF shows peaks at 323.5, 336.4 cm⁻¹ (Fe₂O₃), 474.5, 511.6 cm⁻¹ (NiOOH), 552.4, 665, 698 cm⁻¹ (FeOOH), and 1288 cm⁻¹ (CO₃²⁻).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 5i. The Raman spectra after the HER reaction are less intense than before... More peaks appear in the Raman spectra after the OER. The two peaks at 323.5 and 336.4 cm⁻¹ correspond to Fe₂O₃, and the three peaks at 474.5 and 511.6 cm⁻¹ are attributed to NiOOH. New vibrational peaks appear at 552.4, 665, and 698 cm⁻¹, corresponding to the characteristic Raman peaks of FeOOH... The vibrational peak at 1288 cm⁻¹ can be attributed to the characteristic peak of CO₃²⁻.
